post.description:
Trades the one-time code the OAuth callback gave the native app, plus its PKCE verifier, for a session token.

The code is consumed before the verifier is checked, so a wrong verifier burns it: a guess costs the attacker the code,
and the app just starts the sign-in again. Which check failed is never said.
Login for a native client: the same session as the cookie one, handed back in the body instead of a cookie.

post.description: Starts the reply as a job and streams its events. The job outlives this request: see app/jobs.py.
The only way to stop a reply: the text so far is saved. Does nothing when no reply is running.

get.description:
Replays the events after `Last-Event-ID` (or `?after=`) and follows the reply live.

204 when no reply is buffered, or when `?job=` names a reply that is no longer the chat's current one (the cursor is stale).
